newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SCA SAYS BIDS FOR PWA MINORITY.
newsitem.headline: SCA SAYS BIDS FOR PWA MINORITY.

text.p: Swedish forestry group SCA said on Thursday it bid 335 German marks a share, or a total of about 550 million marks, for outstanding shares in German forestry group Papierwerke Waldhof-Aschaffenburg AG (PWA).
SCA said in a statement the bid would boost its annual net earnings by about one crown a share, based on PWA's six-month earnings.
The bid represents a premium of 23 marks compared with PWA's closing price on Wednesday and can be compared with the 1995 acquisition price of 289 marks per share.
SCA currently owns 75 percent of PWA and holds call options covering about a further 4.6 percent.
"SCA has now decided to establish a so-called domination agreement between SCA and PWA and to make a separate purchase offer to all of PWA's minority shareholders," the company said.

"The domination agreement, which will become effective on January 1, 1998, makes it possible for SCA to control PWA as part of the group and thereby facilitate the continued integration of PWA and SCA," the company said.

This would enable more coordination within the hygiene area where PWA's tissue operations and SCA subsidiary Molnlycke's fluff operations have combined annual sales of about 26 billion crowns, the company said.
The planned integration measures for hygiene operations include a common management organisation, which will be based in the Munich area at year-end.
